review_scope: Complete 94-line article read including metadata, redirects, headings, includes, both fpt conditional boundaries, links and context; all 43 parsed candidates separately accounted in docs-account-policy-artifacts.json. Included fragments independently reviewed in this batch. Source procedures are not executable instructions or applied settings. No actual user/organization policy, current external terms, rendered-version review, rights/adoption or independent omission certification.

claims.statement: The individual-policy article declares Pro, Pro+, Max and Free subscription scope; actual subscription and Student applicability cannot be inferred from this list.
Article version scope uses the Copilot feature, whose separately reviewed pin declares fpt/ghec, not GHES.
GitHub-hosted personal Copilot settings are separate from IDE plugin configuration and are described as applying wherever Copilot is used.
An organization-assigned GHEC Copilot seat removes the personal account's ability to configure public-code suggestions.
For such organization-assigned seats, public-code suggestion policy is inherited from organization or enterprise; personal UI absence is not a missing effective control.
Personal account policy offers separate Allow and Block choices for suggestions matching publicly available code.
Blocking in most Copilot products compares suggestions plus about 150 surrounding-code characters against public code; this is not exhaustive license detection.
With Block selected and a supported product, a public-code match or near match suppresses the suggestion; support and effective settings must be verified.
Allow mode or a product without Block support permits viewing public-code match details and navigating to source repositories; displaying matches does not clear rights.
Public-code policy configuration requires navigating the included Copilot-settings path and selecting Allow or Block; reading the procedure is not observing an applied setting.
Cloud agent supports assignment to issues and autonomous repository research, planning or code changes; described capability is not authorization for those actions.
Cloud agent can create a pull request when the user is ready; autonomous task execution does not make PR creation or merge automatic acceptance.
Cloud-agent availability is delegated to a gating reusable; entitlement and excluded repositories must be reconciled before interpreting defaults.
The article describes cloud agent as enabled in repositories by default, subject to separately included paid-plan and repository exclusions; no target state is observed.
A personal account owner can block cloud agent for repositories owned by that account; this does not grant organization or enterprise policy authority.
Cloud-agent repository controls are accessed through the Cloud agent sidebar; navigation alone does not enforce access.
Repository-access choices are No repositories, All repositories and Only selected repositories; scope is an explicit effective-policy dimension.
Only selected repositories requires choosing an explicit repository set; the mode alone is insufficient proof of restricted access.
The account article includes separate organization/enterprise enablement rules; business licensing is not governed solely by personal repository settings.
Third-party agents, web search and training sections are guarded by the fpt conditional; do not treat their rendered visibility as universal across products.
Third-party coding-agent availability uses the paid-plan permission reusable; article scope listing Free does not establish free third-party agent entitlement.
The article lists Anthropic Claude and OpenAI Codex as third-party coding-agent choices; available choice is not an enabled agent.
Installed agent apps appear under Partner agents and use the same enabling procedure for personal accounts; organization controls can differ.
Partner coding agents inherit cloud agent's enabled repository access set; enabling a partner agent is not a separate unrestricted repository grant.
Partner-agent enablement uses the account cloud-agent settings page and a per-agent toggle; no target toggle has been changed or verified.
Personal Copilot Chat web search is described as disabled by default; observed effective state is required instead of assuming the default.
Enabling web search permits Bing search for information related to the user's question; hosting privacy guarantees alone do not cover this additional processing route.
The Copilot access to Bing dropdown separately controls Enabled or Disabled; this is distinct from model choice and public-code policy.
The included model-training policy supplies plan scope, effective date, data types and authorization caveats; the include link is not itself complete privacy assurance.
The described individual training opt-out is selecting Disabled for Allow GitHub to use my data for AI model training; no active opt-out or propagation receipt is provided.
An absent training dropdown should trigger account/license verification, not PASS or automatic assumption of opted-out individual status.
The article explains the training control is hidden for Business/Enterprise licenses because of stated DPA protection; actual terms and customer authorization require separate evidence.
The view/change-plan article is the linked route for verifying account type; a personal policy page alone does not prove subscription identity.
